README:
The order to acquire the twenty-four crossword books that tools/data/book_candidates.json ranks ACQUIRE and that are not on disk yet. Written 2026-09-19 against tools/data/books.json: every book_index here is a row of that registry, and tools/acquire_book.py refuses an archive.org identifier the registry does not carry, so a row of this file is a command that runs unattended or does not run at all. The volume each book prints on itself lives in the registry and nowhere else; what is kept here is the EVIDENCE for it, in volume_evidence.

ORDER IS EXPECTED USABLE PUZZLES, best first: estimated_puzzle_count multiplied by the fraction of sampled puzzles that passed grid_verdict.screen_spec, both taken from the candidates file. Neither number is a promise — its own README says estimated_puzzle_count runs high because front matter and solution pages print no puzzles, and the two books already acquired came in at 1.2x and 2.3x under their estimates. Rank on it; do not budget on it.

VOLUMES ARE THE BOOK'S OWN NUMBER, twenty-two of twenty-four, and every one of those was read off the item's cover scan rather than off a catalogue: archive.org and Open Library between them had lost the number on five of these books and invented none, so five volumes here are numbers no catalogue will tell you. The word counts as the number — "The First Penguin Book of the Independent Crosswords" is volume 1, "The Ninth Penguin book of the Times crosswords" is volume 9. volume_evidence on each row says which kind of evidence it is, in those words.

TWO VOLUMES ARE INVENTED, and both say so: morse volume 1 (Chambers Book of Morse Crosswords) and brainsharp volume 1 (the Telegraph's Brain Sharpener omnibus). Neither book prints a number anywhere, and neither belongs to a line that numbers its books, so there is nothing a 1 here could contradict. An invented number is never put into a line that does number its books: that is why the Brain Sharpener is not telbig 7.

ONE COLLISION, AND IT IS REAL. Two books on this list are catalogued "The Times Cryptic Crossword Book 21". They are different books: one is Times Books, 1998, ISBN 1-902254-06-7, 144 pages, and its cover reads "THE TIMES CROSSWORDS ... BOOK 21"; the other is HarperCollins, 2017, ISBN 978-0-00-817388-3, and its cover reads "Times Cryptic Crossword Book 21". The HarperCollins run is one volume a year with no gap in it — 12 in 2008 through 29 in 2025 — so 1998 cannot be a renumbering of it. They are two rows of tools/data/books.json, both at volume 21, and each carries the title its own cover prints so no page can name the wrong one.

THIS FILE GOES STALE THE WAY THE CANDIDATES FILE DOES: a book that loses its scan, or a loan pool that empties, changes what a row can do, not what it says. Re-read the item before deciding a failed row is a bug.

acquire_in_this_order.title: The Daily Telegraph Big Book of Brain Sharpener Cryptic Crosswords, volume 1
acquire_in_this_order.volume_evidence: INVENTED. The cover reads "The Daily Telegraph / BIG BOOK OF / BRAIN SHARPENER / CRYPTIC CROSSWORDS" with no number on it, and "Brain Sharpener" was a 2007 Pan sub-brand across puzzle types rather than a numbered crossword line, so there is nothing for this to be the second of.
